method: Automated sweep of Chan's numeral database (CLDF release via numeralbank). Our languages were matched to Chan entries by exact normalised name, preferring an entry whose country list includes Nigeria. Numerals 1-10 come from the first listed variant. Five name matches were rejected outright as different languages on other continents: bina (Bina, Papua New Guinea (Austronesian)); lau (Lau, Solomon Islands (Austronesian)); mangas (Mantsi, Vietnam/China (Sino-Tibetan)); panyam (Mak, China (Tai-Kadai)); ukelle (Kélé, Gabon — different Atlantic-Congo language).
IMPORTANT: These are PHONETIC TRANSCRIPTIONS (IPA), not practical orthography, and must NOT be copied into wordComparison.json as-is. Chan writes Yoruba 'two' as 'eéɟì' where the app displays 'èjì', and Hausa 'two' as 'bíjú' where the app displays 'biyu'. Converting to each language's working orthography is per-language linguistic work needing a speaker or a grammar, not a global find-and-replace. Entries with status='crosscheck' already have a value in the app and are here so a reviewer can confirm the existing form, not replace it. Anything with a 'review' block needs a human decision before use.

source.citation: Chan, Eugene (eds.) 2019. Numeral Systems of the World's Languages. https://mpi-lingweb.shh.mpg.de/numeral
